lessons.title: WAEC Lexis: People, Society and Public Life

description.text: Learn domain vocabulary by reading the situation, identifying the field and testing the natural collocation.

lessons.subject: english-language

objectives.statement: Identify the field of activity signalled by a group of words.
Choose vocabulary that naturally fits the field and sentence context.

text.text: The magistrate dismissed the case after hearing the evidence. Words such as magistrate, case and evidence point to law, so a vocabulary option from agriculture or transport would be a poor fit even if it is a familiar word.

WAEC may place vocabulary in building, agriculture, fishing, health, environment, culture, law, travel, government, sports or religion. You do not need to memorise disconnected lists. Identify the activity, notice the surrounding collocations and decide whether the expression suits a formal or informal situation.

content.alt: Examples of vocabulary fields and contextual clues.

prompt.text: The doctor made a _____ after examining the patient's symptoms: diagnosis, verdict, harvest or fare.

steps.description: The situation is medical, not legal, agricultural or transport-related.
Diagnosis is the natural collocation for identifying an illness.
The field and the word partnership agree.

answer.text: Diagnosis is correct: a doctor makes a diagnosis after examining symptoms.

text.text: If you know the field but ignore the sentence, you can still choose a related wrong word. Test the collocation in full.

points.text: Identify the activity before choosing a word.
Check the natural partnership and register.

prompt.text: Irrigation, seedlings and harvest belong mainly to which vocabulary field?

feedback.text: All three words describe farming and crop production, so agriculture is the field clue.
A judge delivers a verdict. The other options belong to agriculture or medicine.

hint.text: Which word belongs to a court decision?

summary.text: Domain vocabulary becomes useful when learned in a situation and collocation.

lessons.title: WAEC Lexis: Science, Industry and Commerce

description.text: Read technical and business vocabulary through the process, object and relationship it describes.

lessons.subject: english-language

objectives.statement: Use process and object clues to interpret technical vocabulary.
Distinguish natural finance, advertising, manufacturing and commerce collocations.

text.text: The engineer inspected the pipes before the building was occupied. The sentence points to construction and plumbing; the correct word must describe a material, process or fault in that system.

Science and commerce fields include science and technology, animal husbandry, advertising, building, plumbing, finance, photography, mineral exploration, manufacturing, publishing and the stock exchange. Identify what is being made, measured, sold, inspected or communicated. Then test the option's word class and normal partnership.

prompt.text: The company launched an _____ campaign to introduce its new product: advertising, excavation, diagnosis or irrigation.

steps.description: The situation is commercial communication, not mining, medicine or farming.
Advertising naturally modifies campaign in this context.

answer.text: Advertising is correct because a company uses an advertising campaign to promote a product.

content.alt: Process clues for technical and commerce vocabulary.

text.text: A technical word becomes clear through what it does, what it is made of and what words surround it. Do not learn it as an isolated label.

points.text: Identify the process or object first.
Use field, word class and collocation together.

prompt.text: A camera's lens, exposure and shutter belong mainly to:

feedback.text: Lens, exposure and shutter are photography terms.

hint.text: Which activity uses a lens and shutter?

prompt.text: A company paid a broker to buy shares. This belongs chiefly to:

feedback.text: Broker and shares are clues from the stock-exchange field.

hint.text: Where are shares bought and sold?

summary.text: Technical vocabulary is decoded through the process and relationships around it.

lessons.title: WAEC Lexis: Media, Transport, Power and Institutions

description.text: Use setting, participants and purpose to interpret vocabulary from public systems and communication.

lessons.subject: english-language

objectives.statement: Identify a public or communication field from participants and purpose.
Choose a word that fits the institutional context and sentence relationship.

text.text: The editor checked the proofs before the newspaper went to press. Editor, proofs and press identify publishing; a word from air transport or power production would fail the setting.

The remaining WAEC domains include printing and publishing, sea/road/rail/air transport, government and politics, sports and entertainment, power production, education, communication and the military. Identify the institution or system, then ask what role the subject plays: message, movement, energy, authority or performance.

prompt.text: The journalist verified the story with two independent _____. Choose sources, engines, carriages or turbines.

steps.description: The context is reporting and verification.
Sources are people or records from which information comes.
The other options belong to transport or power production.

answer.text: Sources is correct because journalists verify information through sources.

content.alt: Clues for public systems and institutions vocabulary.

text.text: When a word is unfamiliar, use the participants, object and purpose of the situation to locate its field before consulting the options.

points.text: Use setting and participants to identify the field.
Choose the role that completes the institutional relationship.

prompt.text: Curriculum, learner and assessment belong mainly to:

feedback.text: Those words describe teaching and learning, so they belong to education.

hint.text: Which system has learners and assessment?

prompt.text: The electricity company increased power _____ during the heatwave.

feedback.text: Power generation is the production of electrical energy; the other options belong to unrelated fields.

hint.text: What does a power company increase?

summary.text: Public-system vocabulary becomes clear through setting, role and purpose.
